label: Minimal-shape cold start + hot path (default budget)
subject: samples/MinimalApp

notes.coldStartMs: Baseline 420 ms is the minimum of six Release boots of samples/MinimalApp on a QUIET 2026-09-12 dev machine (420/445/456/458/459/477). The same six boots on the SAME machine under load measured 1378/1461/1599/1645/2388/2564 - min 1378, over 3x the quiet minimum. That second run is why the ceiling is 6000 and not Phase 16's 2000: 2 s was measured once by hand on a deployment target and is a fine claim about a deployment, but as a CI ceiling on a shared runner it would flake, and a gate that flakes is a gate people disable. 6000 is ~14x the quiet baseline and ~4.4x the loaded one.
notes.hotPathMs: 5 ms against a 0.36 ms quiet baseline is deliberately ~14x slack; the loaded run measured min 0.688 ms (median 5.6 ms, which is why the gate reads min and not median). These ceilings exist to catch an ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE regression - a default path that starts doing I/O, a middleware registered unconditionally, a per-request allocation storm - not a percent-level one. Slack that has gone stale is not left to anyone's memory: every green run prints the measured headroom ratio, and ToolUp.Platform.Build.Tests refuses a ceiling more than 20x its recorded baseline.
notes.statistic: Wallclock noise on a shared runner is one-sided - a neighbouring job can only make a boot slower - so the minimum over N runs is the least contaminated estimate, and the only statistic whose spread does not widen as the runner gets busier.
notes.absentAssemblies: The zero-cost-when-unused invariant (GP 13, and the Phase 9y 'default-on DROPPED' conclusion) made byte-level rather than timed. A companion nobody registered should not be in the deployment at all - which is checkable exactly, where 'costs no measurable time' is not.
notes.reviewing-a-change: Raising a ceiling is a claim that the SDK is now legitimately slower. Say why in this block, in the same diff.
